what: What the pinned edge-runtime (v1.77.4) event worker receives, measured in one throwaway container launched with the production flags (cap-drop ALL, no-new-privileges, read only root, 32m noexec tmpfs, unprivileged user, 384m, 0.5 CPU) with `--event-worker /home/deno/event` and four functions (talk: console.log and console.error, burn: 40 million loop iterations, boom: throws in the handler, heap: allocates 2 million strings), each called once or twice through the real lab/functions/main. The event worker only printed what it received. Removed afterwards.
findings: A Boot event carries boot_time in ms; a Log event carries msg and level (Info, Error) with the function's service_path and an execution_id; a handler that throws is a Log at level Error with the stack, not an UncaughtException event.

A Shutdown event comes when the worker is dropped, here reason EarlyDrop about 75 seconds after its last call, with cpu_time_used in ms and memory_used total, heap and external in bytes. The numbers are per worker lifetime (the burn function that ran a 40 million iteration loop shows 65 ms against 9 to 18 ms for the others) and memory is what the worker held at shutdown, not its peak: the heap function shows no more than the others.

The event worker can read the container's environment (SB_JWT_SECRET is there; user workers get only the variables the main service passes) and can open connections, so it can send what it learns to the main service with a token only it can sign. Its first connection to 127.0.0.1:9000 was refused because the main service was not listening yet: it must retry.
No event was seen for a worker that is still serving: CPU and memory arrive after the worker ends, so a function that is called all day on one worker reports nothing until that worker is dropped.
not_established: Shutdown for the wall clock timeout and for a worker killed for memory or CPU (reasons other than EarlyDrop)
